4.ask: Cut a line from a list you're carrying — the one that doesn't serve what you're after. Leave it struck where you'll see it for a few days.
4.core:
You've been moving through uncertainty without forcing it, and the account says the way opened, or the timing was off, or circumstances did it. The navigating is happening. The name on it is not.

Not-signing can spread into what you carry: what you keep, what you set down. Take a list, a schedule, a standing habit, and cut the line that doesn't serve what you're after. One line. Keep it where you'll see it a few days with that line gone. Sorting what matters from what doesn't is the skill you've been using; marking the cut as yours is the smaller step.
4.sheetLine: You've been steering this, and calling it the current.

1.tense: The imagining has filled out and it stands here finished, waiting on you.
1.verb: letting what was fully imagined come out satisfied
1.place: where who you are gets to show
1.ask: Keep moving at the pace that made the finished piece — same hours, same order, no pushing for more than the week holds.
1.core:
Something you pictured a while back is mostly built now, and you can feel it. When you talk about it, your voice settles; the strain is no longer in the making. What sits finished here knows how to keep a pace, and it gets used rather than fussed over.

What feeds this is steady motion, not one big push. Find the rhythm you already have and stay in it this week — the speed you could keep for a month, not the one you could keep for a day. Nothing needs to get faster for it to hold. You are building the thing and yourself along with it, and both are going fine.
1.sheetLine: The thing is built and it is still building you.

2.tense: The next version is already being pushed into shape before this one has been stood in.
2.verb: letting what was fully imagined come out satisfied
2.place: where who you are gets to show
2.ask: Pick the piece that is actually working and look after exactly that — feed it, keep it clean, leave the rest alone.
2.core:
You are already designing the next thing, and the next after that, while what you have is still finding its feet. Care has turned into grip. The work gets handled faster than it can grow, and the handling is why nothing settles long enough to count. What is imagined will arrive when it is ready, not when you have checked on it again.

Growth does not need forcing. Pick the one piece that is working and tend that alone. Same hands, same close attention, no extra grip. Tended and left alone at the same time, it will hold better than anything you could push — and the week will tell you which of the rest is worth your hands at all.
2.sheetLine: You're shaping the next one before this one can stand.

3.tense: What you pictured has stopped being felt, and the door you walked through is behind you now.
3.verb: letting what was fully imagined come out satisfied
3.place: where who you are gets to show
3.ask: Take an afternoon and put both sides of what you understand about your own work — what it gives, what it costs — on a single page. Then close it.
3.core:
The imagining went quiet and it has not come back. You understand more than you have said about what you are making, and it sits there unwritten, half of it unadmitted. The feeling went somewhere you stopped looking, and where you are is still answering to the person who had not yet decided anything.

Knowledge does not need to be announced. Sit with both sides of one true thing — what is here and what is not — and write them plainly, no verdict. Then close the page. Something you have understood for a while will be easier to stand next to, and you will have stopped arguing with what you already see.
3.sheetLine: You know it, and it hasn't gotten said.

4.tense: You are keeping the thing steady while calling it luck and someone else's doing.
4.verb: letting what was fully imagined come out satisfied
4.place: where who you are gets to show
4.ask: Look over what is on your plate and take one thing off it — put it down or hand it back — because it does not belong to what you are making.
4.core:
You decided most of what is around you — what got kept, what got dropped, what got said and when. You sort what matters from what does not, quietly, and your account of it is that things landed this way on their own. The people who have watched it land do not share that account.

Distinguishing is not fretting when it is yours to do. Look at the plate, notice the one thing that does not belong to what you are becoming, and take it off — handed back, dropped, unscheduled. You are already the one deciding. Taking one thing off the pile is just that decision letting itself show.
4.sheetLine: The hand picking what stays is yours.

1.tense: You are here, and what you imagined has been felt all the way through.
1.verb: imagining something through to its full felt completion
1.place: standing outside a whole system while still inside it
1.ask: Take the part of the picture you'd reach for anyway. Work it at a speed that feels good to work at, and stop while it still feels good — no finish line on it.
1.core:
You can stand outside a whole thing and still be inside it, and what you imagined you have now felt to the end of. The satisfaction isn't counted — it's the plain fact that the shape is complete enough to stand in, which is what the ninth of anything means.
Moving at the pace your feeling can carry is what keeps this steady. Pick the piece you'd reach for anyway, do it at the speed you could hold for a month rather than for a day, and make pace and direction one motion. Then stop while it still feels good, and tomorrow the rhythm carries itself.
1.sheetLine: The picture is whole, and the pace you keep is your own.

2.tense: You will still be working the finished thing long after it has already ripened.
2.verb: imagining something through to its full felt completion
2.place: standing outside a whole system while still inside it
2.ask: Look at one finished thing you keep handling. This week, tend nothing there — no upgrades, no check-ins. Then look and see how it stands.
2.core:
The vision is whole and the satisfaction is real, and some part of you can't stop attending to it. You keep cultivating past the point where anything needs you, and the work has begun to weigh more than the growing did. From where you stand you can see the whole pattern — and from where you stand you also can't stop reworking it.
Care that doesn't exhaust is the way back, and it looks like holding a thing without clutching it. Let one finished piece stay exactly as it ended this week. What grows after that grows because it was tended, not gripped, and your arms will tell you the difference by the weekend.
2.sheetLine: It's done. Your hands are still on it.

3.tense: You were one step from a finished thing and you stayed at the edge.
3.verb: imagining something through to its full felt completion
3.place: standing outside a whole system while still inside it
3.ask: Set two things you know about the pattern on one page, each its own line, neither one the verdict, then shut the page. Open it later and read both again without picking a winner.
3.core:
You stand where the whole thing is visible, and you haven't stepped in. The imagining went far and the feeling didn't follow it to the end, so you live at the edge now, at the place where nothing has to be declared. From outside the system you see a great deal. From outside it you commit to nothing.
A quieter knowing charges this. Put the two things you see on one page this week, both true, neither winning yet, and shut the page on both of them. Knowing doesn't have to argue to be real, and the reading you were avoiding turns out to be a page you can close.
3.sheetLine: You saw the whole thing and stayed at the edge of it.

1.tense: The imagining has been felt through, and the satisfaction has already arrived in it.
1.verb: feeling what you imagined all the way to the end of it
1.place: the point where one thing is finished enough to leave by
1.ask: Take the work you are deepest in and carry it this week at a rate your own feeling can hold past a month — no surge on it, no stall.
1.core:
The work under your hands is finished enough to trust, and the making and the feeling are running level. What you imagined, you have felt to the far end of, and the calm is not a prize at the finish — it is the temperature of the room. No force is on anything, and nothing is left sitting.

Keeping that rhythm is the work now. Your feeling sets the direction, and taking it faster than it can go is what breaks it. Stay with the one piece and carry it at a rate you could hold a month out, and the momentum belongs to you rather than to the urgency.
1.sheetLine: You move at the pace your feelings can carry.

2.tense: A completion is being forced, and the imagining is being driven to arrive ahead of itself.
2.verb: feeling what you imagined all the way to the end of it
2.place: the point where one thing is finished enough to leave by
2.ask: Tend the thing you keep driving to done: give it what it actually needs, at the rate it is actually moving, and keep your hands open.
2.core:
There is something in your hands you keep bringing toward done before it is ripe, and each push needs another push. The satisfaction you are reaching for stays a step past your fingertips. The imagining is real; the timing is what got forced. What is growing here does not need more will — it needs care at the rate it actually moves.

Let up on the demand and stay close to the thing. Give it steady attention, what it needs when it needs it, without gripping it into a shape before it is ready. Hands that don't clutch and care that doesn't exhaust allow a thing to come to its own ending. Then the finish arrives because it arrived, not because you argued it into being.
2.sheetLine: You are finishing something before it has grown.

4.tense: The weighing of what is done is already yours, and you are calling it luck.
4.verb: feeling what you imagined all the way to the end of it
4.place: the point where one thing is finished enough to leave by
4.ask: When you catch yourself weighing what is worth keeping and what isn't, go slower than usual until the judging hand is visible — then decide and know you decided.
4.core:
The call on when a thing is finished and what to carry forward is already in your hands, and you don't count it as yours. You speak of it as something that simply became clear. There is craft in that weighing — which made thing is worth bringing into what comes next, and which has already given what it had. The craft is running. It is not signed.

Hone the attention rather than the output. The next time you find yourself weighing a finished piece and its worth, slow the moment down until you can see the hand doing the weighing. Sort carefully, and stay aware while you do. Doing it knowingly changes nothing about the work and everything about whose it is.
4.sheetLine: You are judging what is done. Say so.
